PLAN 11A | RUNNING TOWARD THE CAMERA
DURATION 15 SECONDS | HORIZONTAL 16:9
ONE CONTINUOUS HANDHELD SHOT

CHARACTER REFERENCES
{{CHAR_YOUNGER_ESCAPE}} @Townsfolk Masked (look 10) 

LOCATION REFERENCES
{{LOC_ESCAPE_EXTERIOR}}

PROP REFERENCES
{{PROP_ESCAPE_ROBE}}

Create one continuous 15-second horizontal 16:9 cinematic shot following the fleeing Younger Brother FROM THE FRONT.

Preserve his exact referenced identity, handmade mask, original clothing and escape covering. The covering remains draped and secured exactly as shown in the reference, leaving the same areas of his mask and face visible.

His mask is a rigid physical object fixed to his head. Its features and eye openings retain their shape. Fear and grief are performed through visible eyes, breath, head movement, shoulders and running effort.

LOCATION AND LIGHT

An open, uneven plain beyond the rear of the palace complex, before sunrise.

Cold blue-gray skylight softly illuminates the landscape and the front of the running man. The distant rear buildings and city remain behind him, visible in the background whenever framing allows.

The mountains and his escape destination lie behind the camera.

Preserve restrained exposure, tactile clothing, faint moisture on exposed skin and natural movement of the escape covering in the wind.

START STATE AND CAMERA GEOMETRY

The Younger Brother is already running away from the city.

The camera is directly AHEAD of him, facing BACK toward him and the distant city.

His face, chest and front shoulders face the camera throughout.

He runs forward toward the retreating lens. The operator moves backward along the same escape route, matching his speed while allowing the distance to fluctuate naturally.

Begin in a MEDIUM SHOT, framed approximately from his waist upward, using a 40mm lens.

Keep his body near the center with imperfect lateral drift. He looks along his escape route, past the camera, rather than performing to the lens.

SHOT 11A-01 | 00s to 15s | 15 seconds

00–04s:
Track backward at his running speed.

His chest heaves. His arms pump unevenly; one hand briefly catches the escape covering against his chest before releasing it to run again.

The camera bounces with the operator’s backward footfalls. Small corrections keep his masked face readable as he drifts toward either side of the frame.

His breathing is already broken by exhaustion and crying.

04–08s:
He searches the ground ahead with quick downward glances, then looks past the camera toward the open escape route.

One step lands badly. His torso pitches forward, but he catches his balance and continues running.

The camera retreats unevenly in response, briefly letting him come closer. Focus slips toward the near edge of his covering, then recovers on his mask and visible eyes.

His fear remains mixed with grief: a breath catches in his throat, his shoulders tighten and his next exhale becomes a restrained sob.

08–12s:
The operator loses a little distance as the runner closes the gap.

The framing naturally tightens into a MEDIUM CLOSE-UP, from upper chest to head, through the changing physical distance.

His head remains oriented forward. His eyes briefly search to one side of the lens, then return to the route ahead.

Wind presses the covering against one shoulder and pulls its loose edge backward. Preserve the weight and drag of the fabric.

12–15s:
He forces himself through another burst of running despite his failing breath.

The camera regains his pace and holds the close frontal framing with visible handheld effort.

Let his shoulders rise and fall unevenly. His face remains forward, his attention beyond the lens, his body struggling to keep moving.

End while both the runner and camera are still moving.

CAMERA AND PERFORMANCE

The operator is running backward, physically struggling to hold the image.

Use irregular footfall bounce, short lateral corrections and brief focus delays. Recover focus promptly on the mask and visible eyes.

The movement stays urgent and human. His running is exhausted and uneven, driven by fear rather than athletic confidence.

END STATE AND EDIT

The Younger Brother continues running toward the mountains, front-facing to the retreating camera.

His mask, escape covering and clothing remain unchanged.

This is frontal editorial coverage of an ongoing escape. End on active running so the shot can cut into rear coverage or another moment along the route.

SOUND

Close broken breathing.
Restrained nonverbal sobs.
Uneven shoes striking the ground.
Wind pulling at heavy fabric.
The covering rubbing against his chest and arms.
Distant exterior ambience behind the close bodily sounds.

NO MUSIC. NO DIALOGUE.
